papers.title: Efficiently Serving Large Multimodal Models Using EPD Disaggregation
papers.version_note: PD elasticity survey addition; findings bound to this local artifact. Conference-layout PDF from official proceedings or author institution.
papers.reading_scope: Focused reading of relevant paragraphs on the listed physical pages, plus front matter and selected evaluation conditions; not a claim to have reviewed every page or proof.

observations.finding: Simulator/BO configuration optimization and queue-driven online E/P/D role switching. Offload redistributes queued work, Migration changes model/cache as needed, Onload resumes admission. Authors report the process typically below 0.7 s.
100 requests change from 50 to 500 output tokens after request 10 at 3 r/s; 5E1P2D becomes 2E1P5D. Reported mean latency is 28.01 versus 61.10 s, TPOT 0.05 versus 0.12 s, with/without switching.

papers.title: TokenScale: Timely and Accurate Autoscaling for Disaggregated LLM Serving with Token Velocity
papers.version_note: Pinned author arXiv v2 (2026-11-04). Front matter labels SoCC 2026 Volume 2 (2026-11-18 to 2026-11-20), DOI 10.1145/3828161.3857885. Official SoCC program lists TokenPipe: Stage-aware Autoscaling for Disaggregated LLM Serving with Token Velocity with the same author group; title mapping is unresolved. Retained outside the independently matched venue table.
papers.reading_scope: Focused reading of relevant paragraphs on the listed physical pages, plus front matter and selected evaluation conditions; not a claim to have reviewed every page or proof.

observations.finding: Pinned v2 dated 2026-11-04 identifies SoCC 2026 Volume 2 and DOI 10.1145/3828161.3857885. Official program has TokenPipe with matching author group but a different title; title mapping is unresolved, so not counted as an independently matched TokenScale venue identity.

Token velocity drives stage-specific autoscaling; Convertible Decoders execute bounded chunked prefill plus decode. Unlike v1, v2 periodically adjusts convertible decoder count from sliding-window burst estimates. Main workload scope is single-turn, with affinity left for extension.

Author reports AMD MI308X and NVIDIA A100 multi-node RDMA testbeds and allocation from a fixed-size provider GPU pool; unallocated devices remain standby or may serve other out-of-scope workloads. AMD runtime/software mapping is not independently reproduced.

papers.title: FluidPD: In-Place Elasticity for SLO-Aware Prefill-Decode Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.version_note: PD elasticity survey addition; findings bound to this local artifact. Pinned author arXiv v1; publication identity verified independently where listed.
papers.reading_scope: Focused reading of relevant paragraphs on the listed physical pages, plus front matter and selected evaluation conditions; not a claim to have reviewed every page or proof.

observations.finding: FluidToken offloads bounded prefill suffixes; FluidRole changes running workers with PPI/DPI signals. ACTIVE-DRAIN-SWITCH retains process, weights and model-parallel groups. Queued work is reassigned; active P and KV sends or active D generations drain. First decode graph capture is cached. Persistence, minimum-drain selection and cooldown guide changes.

Testbed is one AWS server with eight A100-80GB GPUs and NVLink, one GPU per instance; SGLang v0.5.4, three models and Azure-derived staged/mixed traces. Fixed GPU comparisons are distinct from the 6-to-8 autoscaling comparison.

Authors report below 0.50 ms CPU control iteration, about 1 s P-to-D and up to 12 s D-to-P under tested conditions. D-to-P completion waits for existing active sequences, not Llumnix-style live request migration.

papers.title: HFX: Joint Design of Algorithms and Systems for Multi-SLO Serving and Fast Scaling
papers.version_note: Author arXiv v3, pinned after checking the current arXiv history on 2026-11-06; venue identity is verified separately where available. Originally titled HyperFlexis in v1/v2; this review uses HFX v3.
papers.reading_scope: Focused reading of relevant paragraphs on the listed physical pages, plus front matter and selected evaluation conditions; not a claim to have reviewed every page or proof.

observations.finding: Pinned v3 dated 2026-04-23 is titled HFX, replacing HyperFlexis from v1/v2.

Separate stage scalers can reassign roles. Python-runtime-only warm-up pool, HCCL D2D weights with disk fallback, and pre-established KV link groups prepare instances before serving. Backend is vLLM-Ascend with Ascend 910B and LLM-DataDist. Process/weight retention across role transitions is not established as fully as FluidPD.

papers.reading_scope: Focused reading of relevant paragraphs on the listed physical pages, plus front matter and selected evaluation conditions; not a claim to have reviewed every page or proof.

observations.finding: Micro-requests can split at token boundaries, extending beyond the fixed prompt boundary. Unified instances use global split/routing and local SLO-aware token budgets; chunk KV transfers overlap computation.
Official NSDI 2026 version is Libra, formerly DynaServe in preprint citations. This survey uses the official version; does not treat unified micro-request execution as pure P/D pool resizing.

papers.title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
papers.reading_scope: Focused reading of relevant paragraphs on the listed physical pages, plus front matter and selected evaluation conditions; not a claim to have reviewed every page or proof.

observations.finding: Goodput-aware placement chooses stage parallelism and replication subject to topology. Replanning detects significant workload shifts, reruns placement using recent history and reloads weights; seconds planning and minutes loading are distinguished.

visual_checks.finding: Read the three-step role-change procedure in correct column order; Table 6 is on physical page 9, not 8. Values and 5E1P2D-to-2E1P5D transition checked.
Figure 8 preserves process, weights and communication groups. Text differentiates queued-request reassignment from active-request drain and describes directional cost.
Section 4.4.2 describes online periodic convertible decoder count adjustment; Section 4.6 states single-turn scope. Hardware paragraph identifies MI308X RDMA setup.

publication_and_version_notes: TaiChi is in the official SC 2026 program for 2026-11-18, after the current 2026-11-06 survey date. Author v1 and program abstract numbers differ; no cross-version performance claim is made.

HFX v3 (2026-04-23) replaces HyperFlexis v1/v2. Arrow v2, DOPD v3, TokenScale v2, HFX v3 and LoongServe v2 were selected after current arXiv history checks.

Feature matrix is a scoped synthesis of these passages. Partial/uncovered labels refer to the inspected mechanisms; Ours denotes unimplemented design goals and is not evidence of novelty or measured benefit.

research_synthesis.finding: Compare reserve-first versus drain-first in-place role changes at fixed total resources; jointly measure reserve occupancy/recovery, transition stage cost and cumulative SLO delivery, alongside mixed/unified execution and active-migration alternatives.
